newsitem.title: CANADA: Oil companies reject Quebec plan to fix gas price.
newsitem.headline: Oil companies reject Quebec plan to fix gas price.

text.p: Canada's five major oil companies, Ultramar Ltd, Imperial Oil Ltd, Irving Petroleum Inc, Petro-Canada and Shell Canada Ltd, rejected a plan by Quebec to fix gas prices.

Appearing on Wednesday before a legislative committee studying a government bill that would set up a minimum gas price, the oil companies told Quebec's Energy Minister Guy Chevrette that the plan would harm consumers and the industry.

"The adoption of a minimum margin guaranteed for gas retail sale and diesel is unjustified and unnecesssary and could be very expensive for Quebec consumers," Imperial Oil spokesman Claude Larochelle said.
Imperial estimates the measure could cost Quebec consumers up to C$250 million.
Ultramar Canada president Alain Ferland said: "We are against any regulation and we are in favour of free competition,".
Ferland questioned the government's intention to include the oil industry in a new government agency mandate and to regulate its activities.
Quebec plans to create an Energy Board to monitor gasoline prices and prohibit all stakeholders in the oil industry from posting prices at the pump lower than wholesale prices.

The move follows a price war last summer, where gasoline prices in Montreal fell to C$0.19 a litre. Small independent retailers, who represent 16 percent of the market in Quebec, accused the majors of trying to put them out of business.
The government, which has declared its intention to protect the small independent retailers, is expected to pass the legislation before Christmas.
